full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim, J: This appeal at the instance of the plaintiff and directed against the judgment and decree dated 31-3-2009 passed by the learned Judge, Fourth Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka in Artha Rin Mamla No. 159 of 2008 dismissing the suit. 

 5. Further case of the defendant are that the plaintiff-Bank by showing sanction Advice dated 29-5-2005 for an loan amount of Taka 98,00,000 in the name of his business firm, Shovon Enterprise, unnecessary harassing the defendant; that in fact the plaintiff's officials called the defendant on 23-1-2007 and obtained his signature in the sanction Advice; that the loan application dated 14-9-2005 is not signed by the defendants; that from the papers and documents filed by the plaintiff, it shows that before opening of the Bank account by the defendant on 27-9-2005 he applied for Investment loan which is against the rules of the Bank; thus it is obvious that matters of applying investment loan is manufactured/ created by the plaintiff-Bank; that till now the defendant did not make any transaction in the said Bank Account; that a news item was published in several National dailies namely, Prothom Alo, Samakal disclosing the irregularities, forged and fraudulent activities done by the officials of the plaintiff's-Bank, they in connivance with each other and illegally misappropriated crores of money by opening fake accounts by forging the signatures of good numbers of account-holders of the plaintiff-Bank; that when the defendant went to the plaintiff's Branch on 234-2007 he became surprise to know that loan was sanctioned long before in his name. It is also stated that although the defendant did not make any transaction in the loan account but the plaintiff's officials by corrupt practice and manufacturing forged documents was manage to misappropriated huges amount of money by opening several fake Bank Account. In such circumstances the defendant was constrained to filed Title Suit No. 28 of 2007 in the Third Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka against the plaintiff-Bank; that the plaintiff filed the instant suit just to harass the defendant and they are not entitled to get any relief in the present suit. Accordingly, the defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 7. In this suit both the parties examined one witness each and plaintiffs documents were marked as Exhibit-1 to 7(ka). 8. The learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Fourth Court, Dhaka after considering the evidence and materials on record dismissed the suit on the findings that it was admitted by both the parties that BAI-MUAJJAL loan was applied by the defendant on 14-9-2005 but the present Bank account was opened on 27-9-2005 which shows that the defendant applied for loan before opening of the account No. 3300-5589 (Exhibit-3). It was further found that no permission was obtained from the Head Office of the plaintiff-bank which was clearly admitted by the PW 1 and it is the positive case of the defendant that he did not apply for any loan and totally denied the transaction of the loan account. 

 10. Mr Md Hamidur Rahman, the learned advocate appearing for defendant-respondent submits that the plaintiff has miserably failed to prove that alleged loan of Taka 98, 00,000 was sanctioned to the defendant by Sanction Advice dated 29-9-2005 (Exhibit-4). He further submits that clause (d) of the said advice clearly stipulates, if the defendant accepted the terms and conditions, he must sign on the duplicate of the sanction advice and return to the bank as token of acceptance of the loan. But in this suit plaintiff did not file signed Duplicate Copy of the said sanction advice (Exhibit-4) to prove that the defendant has accepted the loan. He  next submits that trial court rightly found Current Account No. 33005589 was opened by the plaintiff on 27-9-2005 with initial deposit of Taka 1,000 but so-called loan application was filed on 14-9-2005 (Exhibit-3), which strongly proved that fraudulent activities of the bank official to the effect that before opening of the bank account by the plaintiff, so-called application of loan (Exhibit-3) was filed and Bank officials created various documents by forging the signatures of the defendant. He has also contended that after publishing news items in different National Dailies about irregularities of the plaintiff's-Bank, the defendant after inquiry, came to learn that a loan amount of Taka 98, 00,000 was sanctioned in his name without his knowledge. Although the defendant did not apply for any loan but the officials and Directors of the Bank in collusion with each other by practicing fraud and forgery, illegally shown sanction of loan in the name of the defendant. Accordingly, the defendant filed a suit being Title Suit No. 28 of 2007 in the Third Joint District Judge, Dhaka. He finally submits that Bangladesh Bank formed a Special Inspection Team to find out of the irregularities committed by the officials and Directors of the Oriental Bank. The said Team on 19-6-2006 conducted inspection and inquiry in the Head Office and 5(five) other branches including the plaintiff-Nawabpur Branch, found that some transaction was shown in the account of the Shovon Enterprise, proprietorship concern of the present defendant-respondent had been deposited in the personal account of Mr Obaidul Karim. On the basis of the report of the Special Inspection Team, the Oriental Bank Ltd. now ICB Islamic Bank Ltd. filed Tejgaon Police Station Case No. 4 of 25-1-2007 under section 120-B/409/416/462-A/462-B/477-A/420 and 109 of the Penal Code. He has finally submitted that the learned trial Judge upon due consideration of the evidence and materials on record rightly dismissed the suit. Accordingly, he prayed that the appeal should be dismissed with heavy cost and the Judgment and decree passed by the trial court should be affirmed. 

 12. It is admitted by both the parties that defendant applied to the Manager, Oriental Bank Ltd., Nawabpur Branch Dhaka for Bi-Moazzal loan facility on 14-9-2005 for Taka 1,00,00,000(one crore) (Exhibit- 3) stating that he maintained one Current Account being No. 3300-5589 in the name of his proprietorship firm, M/s Shovon Enterprise in the said Branch. Admittedly, Defendant filed an application to the plaintiff-Bank on 27-9-2005 for opening Current Account with initial case deposit of Taka 1,000 (Exhibit-2), which shows that defendant filed loan application before opening of the Bank Account. It is really surprising, how the plaintiff mentioned the Current Account No. 3300-5589 in his application of loan dated 14-9-2005 in the name of his Proprietary concern, SHOVON Enterprise, admittedly the said account was opened later on 27-9-2005 (Exhibit-2). It is quiet absurd, unusual and not believable, how the defendant put his said Current Account no in the application filed on 14-9-2005 before opening the account on 27-9-2005. Thus the trial court rightly found that the application for availing loan (Exhibit-3) was created in connivance and practicing fraud by the plaintiff-Bank officials of the said Branch. 

 15. It further transpires that the defendant successfully proved that Gigantic fraud and forgery has been committed by the officials of the Bank and they illegally misappropriated crores of money by corrupt practice. This affairs of the plaintiff-Bank was published in the leading National Dailies and same was admitted by PW 1 in this cross-examination state that “….. ব্যাংকের চেয়ারম্যান ও অন্যান্য কর্মকর্তাদের নামে মামলার কথা পত্রিকার মাধ্যমে শুনেছি। টাকা আত্মসাৎ করার জন্য মামলা হয়েছে বলে জেনেছি। বিভিন্ন পত্রিকায় এই ঘটনা প্রকাশিত হয়েছে ।” Further to find out the irregularities of the plaintiff-Bank, Bangladesh Bank formed a Special Inspection Team and the said Team on 19-6-2006 conducted inspection and inquiry in the Head Office and 5(five) other Branches including the plaintiff, Nawabpur Branch of the Oriental Bank, which was disclosed by the DW 1 in his cross-examination “কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংক তদন্ত করে প্রতিবেদন দিয়েছে যে, কাগজ আমার কাছে আছে।” 

 18. In the result, the appeal is dismissed with cost of Taka 10,000(Ten thousand) only. The Judgment and decree dated 30-3-2009 passed by the Fourth Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka dismissing the Artha Rin Mamla No. 159 of 2008 are hereby affirmed. Send down the lower court record out a copy of judgment be sent to the concerned court at one.
